pr_title: Fix: Fixed closing app when the item flyout is open to hang
pr_body:
**Resolved / Related Issues**
Items resolved / related issues by this PR.
- Closes #10110

**Details**
For some reason, the application does not close properly when a CommandBarFlyout is open, so the open flyout is forced to close before closing app, and then the application is closed as the event after closing the flyout.

**Validation**
How did you test these changes?
- [X] Built and ran the app
- [X] Tested the changes for accessibility

issue_context.title: Bug: Closing app when menu flyouts are open causes hang
issue_context.body:
### Description

Closing the app when the right click content menu is still open causes the application to hang for a couple of seconds before it closes.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Right click on a file or folder
2. Click close button on the title bar
3. Observe that the application hangs for a couple of seconds before closing

### Steps to fix

- Fix hang that occurs when opening the context menu before closing the app

### Files Version

v.2.3.39

### Windows Version

Windows 11

### Relevant Assets/Logs

No crash is detected in the log files
comments: This might be a WinAppSdk issue but it's hard to know.

I can confirm that this is indeed a bug.


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/109022579/195944587-a78b772e-c2df-4596-9ea3-7cebdc897fd7.mp4

review_comments: Should we unsubscribe when it closes?
I think there is no need to do so because a new instance of the flyout is created each time and is not reused.
I think you're right, but can you verify just in case it's doing something weird?
I have verified that the flyout works after showing flyouts several times on the home screen and also that the application exits without issue. Should I still check something?

Memory leaks from not unsubscribing would occur if the publisher continues to remain. But since the publisher is disposed every time, memory leaks should not occur. If a memory leak were to occur, it would happen without subscribing to the event.
